answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents stake tokens across a trust graph layered like a terrace. Verifiers perform topological cut verifications to identify bottlenecks where artificial identity clusters aggregate. In multi-agent auditing, dishonest clusters forfeit collateral via stake slashing. By sampling cut metrics alongside audit scores, the system creates a resilient economic reef that traps spoofed nodes, tagging fraud like an indelible pigment and imposing superlinear attacker cost as graph partition density scales.
